title: Modular curves, following Katz–Mazur, Part II: Uniformization, integral boundary and Hecke cohomology
summary: A complete target-level planning pass for generic-fibre compatibility, bad reduction and geometric Hecke cohomology through finite Taylor–Wiles control. All 75 required targets already have canonical accepted nodes in the R13.3 and R14.3 packets. This packet imports them without creating duplicate nodes, synchronizes the reader with the corrected statements and records the assembly contracts: 35 resolutions of stage citations to exact accepted nodes (including the R12.1 packet’s R12.3, R12.5, R12.6 and R13.2 nodes) and one import of the ReductiveGroupsPartII tree and AdelicAlgebraicGroups strong approximation into R14.4/modular-amalgam. All nine stages are planned, with nine explicit gaps and 38 supplier requests retained. No stage is claimed closed or implemented.

The accepted R12.1 packet states the compact analytic comparison, the cusp-width and Tate-parameter agreement and the cusp-field/determinant-label identification. The consumer adds only the descent by the determinant image of H and the scalar-framed component count.
Canonical generic models, component fields of the full-level curve and compatibility with level maps are exactly these accepted nodes; the last one names R13.4b as its consumer.
Generic-fibre descent by q-expansions and compatibility of the comparisons with level maps, diamonds and characteristic-zero Hecke actions are the R12.6 inputs this comparison uses.

The canonical Q-models of X₀(N) and X₁(N) and the Galois action on cyclotomic Tate-level cusp labels determine the cusp fields; choosing a rational cusp (0 on the point-of-exact-order model, ∞ or 0 on X₀(N)) is the consumer’s computation.

R12.5/perfect-hecke-pairing already proves perfection of β(T,f)=a₁(Tf) on V_Q=H⁰(X₀(N)_Q,Ω¹) for the cotangent Hecke image T_Q. The consumer’s own content is the identification of the Jacobian Hecke image tensored with Q with T_Q by faithfulness of the cotangent action; its nondegeneracy steps are the supplier’s proof and are imported, not proved again.
S₂(Γ)≅H⁰(X,Ω¹) with its cusp and elliptic-point behaviour, and the 2πi dz frame of the Hodge line, are the R12.5 inputs of the Hodge decomposition step.
The normalization f↦2πi f(τ)dτ fixes the forms whose wedge product is computed.

The mixed Γ₁(N;n) level structure (with the disjointness condition [G_d+H_d]=Eˢᵐ[d]), properness and flatness of its stack, its DM/representability range and the contraction maps between levels are these accepted nodes. The refined Γ₀ construction is not an input of this node.
For N≥5 the fine Γ₁(N) curve, smooth after inverting N, with its universal elliptic curve on the elliptic locus (the Katz–Mazur representing scheme) is supplied by these nodes.

Conrad’s proof of Theorem 5.16 needs the smooth proper fine X₁(N) over ℤ[1/N] (good reduction at p∤N) with its moduli interpretation on Y₁(N), and, on the ordinary locus, the connected–étale order-p subgroups of an ordinary curve and of its lifts (ModularCurves 7E PD-2, PD-5). Density of the ordinary locus and lifting of ordinary points follow from smoothness and are steps of the consumer’s proof. The earlier request to R13.2 for these ordinary-locus inputs named the wrong owner.
The point-of-exact-order Γ₁(N) moduli model and its agreement with the Katz–Mazur scheme fix the model on which the rational cusp is chosen.

gaps.title: Wild coarse bad-level interior models at 2 and 3
gaps.detail: The required arbitrary-N Γ₀(pⁿM) component/multiplicity target and R20 cases include p=2,3. Edixhoven’s exact interior invariant-ring/minimal-resolution formulas are proved for p>3. Česnavičius gives all-prime coarse cusp regularity and regularity away from exceptional interior j-values, not the missing wild local equations. Required calculation: use imported cyclic deformation rings, compute the actual finite stabilizer action at level-dividing 2 or 3 (including infinitesimal inertia), identify normal invariant completions and their multiplicities, resolve and export branch/thickness maps. A tame order-2/3 eigencharacter argument is insufficient. The fine rigidified one-p-factor uv=p model is separated from this coarse descent gap.

gaps.title: Relative curve norm and principal polarization contract
gaps.detail: JacobianChallenge D proves the field curve Jacobian. A0-extension supplies relative Picard space, lifting and a neutral-component criterion; it does not by itself supply the curve-specific relative canonical principal polarization/norm theorem over ℤ[1/N]. The request to A0-extension and AbelianSchemes A2 names this exact additional comparison. No fictional relative Jacobian carrier or field-only-to-relative inference is made.

gaps.title: Integral cuspidal-symbol realization contract
gaps.detail: Current ModularForms Layer 8 constructs the full Γ₁-coinvariant module Div⁰(P¹(ℚ))⊗Sym and a Hecke-equivariant period quotient onto the form-side image. It explicitly does not require an isomorphism of its whole module with S_k⊕conj(S_k); boundary/Eisenstein classes and integral torsion must be handled. The local R14.2 comparison target must construct the weight-two cuspidal boundary kernel modulo torsion and identify its integral Hecke action with compact-curve H₁, or the appropriately transposed dual H¹, retaining all diamond and bad-prime conventions. Determine exact kernels at the integral level, rather than inferring them from rational dimensions or period injectivity on forms. The J/Betti/Tate comparison remains separate and justified.

gaps.title: Integral higher-weight boundary and lattice range
gaps.detail: Deligne supplies rational Sym^r cohomology. Prove the exact good-prime Hecke eigensystems on H⁰ and cusp inertia cohomology for Sym^r integral coefficients; specify residual ideals where they vanish and where reduction and saturated parabolic comparison hold. For ℓ≤r symmetrization need not be perfect: choose a divided-power/dual lattice with a sourced comparison or retain a weaker pairing. The present conditional theorem does not claim unconditional integral freeness or perfectness in that range. The symbol comparison must identify the standard representation with the dual geometric relative-H¹ coefficient system, including determinant twists, and prove the Manin/geodesic relative-chain presentation on B. Deligne and the rational even-weight boundary model do not by themselves establish this integral identification.

gaps.title: Deep input to the S-arithmetic congruence kernel theorem
gaps.detail: Serre 1970 §2.6 gives the correct real-place specialization, but its proof depends on central Mennicke-symbol/congruence-kernel calculations and the Moore/class-field-theory input. Those intermediate theorems have not been decomposed against the baseline. A follow-up must supply that exact proof chain; an unrelated profinite arithmetic action theorem cannot replace it.

gaps.title: Tree fundamental edge and enhanced congruence-character proof
gaps.detail: The lattice tree of SL₂(ℚ_p), its type-preserving action without inversion and the local amalgam are imported from ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2/sl2-tree and RG2.2/ihara-amalgam, and strong approximation with reduction surjectivity prime to p from AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4/strong-approximation-sufficiency and AA.4/strong-approximation-finite-places (dependencyAdditions). Still missing for modular-amalgam: Serre’s theorem that a group acting on a tree without inversion with a segment as fundamental domain is the amalgam of the two vertex stabilizers over the edge stabilizer (Trees I §4.1 Theorem 6, p. 48), which ReductiveGroupsPartII uses inside the proof of ihara-amalgam but does not state as a target, and the finite congruence-quotient sublemmas of the principal-level argument. Refine the CDT Corollary 4.5.3 conjugation-invariance criterion against existing finite-group APIs. This is a proof-chain gap, not permission to erase the congruence subspace from ordinary Ihara. For congruence-invariance, supply the exact continuous-cohomology, Künneth and Hochschild–Serre proof interfaces, Lazard’s uniform-group calculation, adjoint-cohomology vanishing, and a reproducible proof of the level-8/16 computations used in CDT §4.5.11. These source inputs are not declarations established by the pinned ordinary H¹ carrier.

gaps.title: Integral modular old/new and quaternionic pivot exactness
gaps.detail: Ribet–Stein §3.10.2 equation (3.2), p. 48 involves a quaternionic Shimura-curve Jacobian J′_{pq}(K). The exact sequence 0→X_p(J′_{pq}(K))→X_q(J(K,pq))→X_q(J(K,q))²→0 needs the specific Cerednik–Drinfeld identification and integral Hecke-compatible maps. Generic Néron functoriality and a rational old/new isogeny do not establish this integral sequence. Keep the conditional torus theorem here; arrange a lower-tier geometric interface before the higher Hilbert/Shimura-curve roadmap consumes it, or explicitly narrow the requested consumer. Retain finite cokernels and component groups until that proof is supplied.

gaps.title: Extensions of the exact Ihara consumer range
gaps.detail: The compact constant-coefficient Γ₁(N) result includes ℓ|N on characteristic-zero curves and has no exceptional residual-image hypothesis. It does not by itself prove level lowering, nor a uniform Sym^r/coarse Γ₀(N) or characteristic-ℓ fibre result. R20/R22 must use the stated fine/mixed-level weight-two prefix, or specify a sourced further injectivity theorem with its stabilizer, coefficient and exceptional-image hypotheses; Γ₀(N) has a Shimura-subgroup kernel.
